summary: Iteration 14 - Admin product reorder feature (up/down arrows in Product Management filtered by category). Backend 12/12 pytest PASS (100%). Frontend reorder flow fully verified end-to-end: hidden when 'All categories' selected, visible+functional when a specific category (Topicals) selected, first-row up disabled, last-row down disabled, swap works, undo restores order. The Topicals category order was restored to its original alphabetical state after testing.

auth_observation.issue: Filling the visible Email/Password fields and clicking Sign In appears to silently redirect to /auth (the public Firebase login) instead of authenticating. POST /api/login works perfectly via curl/fetch (returns valid JWT + isAdmin=true). Workaround used in tests: call /api/login from page.evaluate and seed localStorage('token','auth_token','authToken','access_token','user'), then navigate to /admin/products. Once seeded, the admin UI loads correctly and shows 'Product Management'. Recommend the main agent verify which exact key the React auth provider reads (use-auth.ts) and ensure the /admin-login form persists it correctly. Iteration 13 also relied on a bypass — this is not a new regression but is still worth fixing for true e2e UI auth coverage.

action_items: MEDIUM: Investigate why the /admin-login form submission doesn't persist auth state — UI redirects to /auth after clicking Sign In. POST /api/login works fine; the issue is in the frontend (likely use-auth.ts or admin-login.tsx not storing the returned token under the key the rest of the app reads). Once fixed, end-to-end UI auth tests can run without a localStorage bypass.
INFO: Iteration 13's recurring 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading match)' console error is still present on every route navigation. Non-blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/products.py:198 _normalize_category_order runs N sequential awaits for each product update — for large categories this is O(N) round-trips. Consider bulk_write with UpdateOne operations if categories grow beyond ~50 products. Currently fine for Topicals(10).

routes/products.py:219 move_product does up to 4 awaits (find_one + normalize + 2 updates) without a transaction. Race-condition window: two admins clicking simultaneously could interleave swaps. For an admin-only single-user feature this is acceptable; flag for future when multi-admin orgs land.
routes/products.py:222 direction Query uses pattern='^(up|down)$' which is the FastAPI v2-friendly form. Good. Returns 422 as expected.

product-management.tsx:603 disabled relies on filteredProducts[0]?.id === product.id and filteredProducts[length-1]?.id === product.id — this only works because the filtered list and the backend's sorted list happen to match. If client-side filtering ever diverges from server sort order (e.g., user adds visibility filter on top), the 'first/last' detection could become wrong. Acceptable today.

product-management.tsx:200 moveProductMutation only invalidates ['/api/products'] — does NOT invalidate any category-page or storefront product caches. If admin reorders while a customer has /shop open in another tab, customer won't see the new order until refetch. Minor.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The product reorder feature is fully working backend+frontend. Tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_product_reorder.py and are safe to re-run (the down-then-up sequence is order-preserving). For UI tests against /admin/* pages, currently the most reliable path is: navigate to /, call /api/login via page.evaluate, seed localStorage keys (token, auth_token, authToken, access_token, user), then navigate to the target admin page. rca_of_the_issue: No critical issues. The reorder endpoint correctly normalizes displayOrder to 10/20/30 spacing on first interaction, swaps neighbour values for clean reorder, returns moved:false at list edges, and uses FastAPI Query(pattern=...) for direction validation (yields 422). The TanStack Query invalidation on the frontend correctly refetches and re-renders the table after each move.
